'''David Victor Hinkley''' (10 September 1944 – 11 January 2019) was a [[statistician]] known for his research in [[statistical model]]s and [[statistical inference|inference]] and for his graduate-level books.

==Early life==
David Victor Hinkley was born on 10 September 1944 in [[Kent|Kent, England]].<ref name="obit">{{Cite web |url=https://imstat.org/2019/07/15/obituary-david-hinkley-1944-2019/ |title=Obituary: David Hinkley 1944–2019 |date=2019-07-15 |last=Davison |first=Anthony |website=[[Institute of Mathematical Statistics]] |access-date=2022-01-25}}</ref><ref name="death">{{cite web|last=Yang|first=Henry T.|author2=Department of Statistics and Applied Probability|authorlink=Henry T. Yang|date=31 January 2019|publisher=[[University of California, Santa Barbara]] Office of the Chancellor|title=David Victor Hinkley 1945-2019|url=https://chancellor.ucsb.edu/memos/2019-01-31-sad-news-professor-emeritus-david-hinkley |access-date=2022-01-25}}</ref><ref name="allstat">{{cite web|date=31 January 2019|first1=Anthony|last1=Davison| first2=Nancy|last2=Reid| first3=Valérie|last3=Ventura| title=ALLSTAT Archives: David Hinkley|url=https://www.jiscmail.ac.uk/cgi-bin/webadmin?A2=ind1901&L=allstat&P=221874|website=www.jiscmail.ac.uk}}</ref> He studied mathematics and statistics at the [[University of Birmingham]]. He earned a [[Doctor of Philosophy|PhD]] from the [[University of London]] (now [[Imperial College London]]) in 1969 under the supervision of [[David R. Cox]].<ref name="obit"/><ref>{{Mathgenealogy|id=45589}}</ref>

==Career==
While working on his PhD, Hinkley was appointed to a junior lectureship at the University of London.<ref name="obit"/> He spent the years 1969 to 1971 at [[Stanford University]].<ref name="obit"/> In 1971, he returned to London, and then, in 1973, he moved to the [[University of Minnesota]] where he was a member of the faculty.<ref name="obit"/><ref name="death"/> In 1983, Hinkley moved to the [[University of Texas at Austin]] and became a faculty member.<ref name="obit"/><ref name="death"/> In 1989, he moved to lead the new department of statistics at the [[University of Oxford]].<ref name="obit"/> In 1995, he became a professor at the [[University of California, Santa Barbara]].<ref name="death"/><ref name="obit"/> He also served as chair of the department of statistics and applied probability from 1995 to 2002. He served as the director of undergraduate studies from 2003 to 2007. He retired from UC Santa Barbara in 2014.<ref name="death"/><ref>[http://www.pstat.ucsb.edu/people/david-v-hinkley Faculty webpage]</ref>

In 1974 Hinkley and Cox published ''Theoretical Statistics'', a textbook on statistical inference.<ref name="obit"/> Hinkley also collaborated with [[Bradley Efron]], in particular on writing a paper on [[maximum likelihood|maximizing]] the [[likelihood function#Conditional likelihood|conditional likelihood function]] and on using the [[observed information|observed]] [[Fisher information]].<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Efron   |first1=B.   |authorlink1=Bradley Efron |last2=Hinkley |first2=D.V. <!--|authorlink2=David V. Hinkley --> |year=1978 |title=Assessing the accuracy of the maximum likelihood estimator: Observed versus expected Fisher Information |journal=[[Biometrika]] |volume=65 |issue=3 |pages=457–487 |doi=10.1093/biomet/65.3.457 |mr=0521817 | jstor = 2335893}}</ref> Hinkley was an expert on [[bootstrapping (statistics)|bootstrapping]], a method of [[computational statistics]], which is largely due to Efron.  With [[Anthony C. Davison]], Hinkley wrote a widely used textbook on the subject.<ref>Davison, A. C.; Hinkley, D. (2006). ''Bootstrap Methods and their Application'' (8th printing). Cambridge: Cambridge Series in Statistical and Probabilistic Mathematics</ref>

==Personal life and death==
Hinkley married Betty Blake in 1970. Together, they had two children, Sara and Steve.<ref name="obit"/><ref name="allstat"/> They divorced in 1991.<ref name="obit"/> Hinkley had interests in soccer, nature and classical music.<ref name="obit"/>

Hinkley died on January 11, 2019, at his home in [[Santa Barbara, California]].<ref name="death"/>

==Awards==
Hinkley was an elected fellow of the [[American Statistical Association]], a fellow of the [[Institute of Mathematical Statistics]], fellow of the [[Royal Statistical Society]] and fellow of the [[American Association for the Advancement of Science]]. He was also an honorary fellow at the [[University of Edinburgh]] and a vice president of the Royal Statistical Society.<ref name="death"/>

In 1984 Hinkley received the ''[[COPSS Presidents' Award]]''.<ref name="death"/><ref>[http://www.imstat.org/awards/copss_recipients.htm COPPS Awards – Recipients] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160312212858/http://imstat.org/awards/copss_recipients.htm |date=2016-03-12 }}.</ref>
